stories.title: Fujitsu Research India driving Arm-based software push for MONAKA CPU
stories.summary: Fujitsu’s MONAKA CPU uses a chiplet design: 2nm compute cores 3D-stacked on 5nm I/O and SRAM dies, and can operate at a maximum frequency of 3.8 GHz with a memory transfer speed of 8800 MT/s. Its hardware development and manufacturing are happening in Japan.
stories.content:
NEW DELHI: A top executive of Fujitsu Research India said the company is contributing to the development of Arm-based software stacks for the Japanese conglomerate’s MONAKA central processing unit (CPU), which is geared for data center and artificial intelligence (AI) applications.“From India, we are building the software engineering ecosystem. That means we enable PyTorch, OpenVINO, NumPy, and OneAPI implementations. These are different AI stacks, and our work forms the backbone of AI model performance on CPU,” Priyanka Sharma, director (software engineering) & head (MONAKA software R&D unit), Fujitsu Research of India, told 

*ETElectronicsWorld*in an interview.“We work at the framework engineering level for the Arm ecosystem. So, 90% of our work is focused on kernel optimisation,” she added.Fujitsu’s MONAKA CPU uses a chiplet design: 2nm compute cores 3D-stacked on 5nm I/O and SRAM dies, and can operate at a maximum frequency of 3.8 GHz with a memory transfer speed of 8800 MT/s. Its hardware development and manufacturing are happening in Japan.The company plans to commence global sales of FUJITSU-MONAKA starting in November 2026. This will include sales of the processor as a standalone product to cloud and data center operators and server vendors.“While it is challenging to contribute to the high-performance computing (HPC) side of AI framework engineering for the Arm ecosystem, we are doing it extensively,” Sharma said, adding that there has been a “phenomenal” improvement in Arm’s software ecosystem maturity in the last three years.The Arm ecosystem is underpinned by Arm Holdings, which licenses its chip architecture for applications that prioritise power efficiency, including laptops, tablets, and smartphones. By contrast, the x86 architecture-based Intel and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) products that focus on raw compute have traditionally dominated the personal computer (PC) and enterprise server markets.In recent years, complex instruction set architecture (CISC) x86 offerings have started facing increasing pressure as data center operators and manufacturers pivot to Arm-based architectures due to their lower energy consumption and total cost of ownership (TCO) advantages.The maturing Arm ecosystem has also attracted the US-based Qualcomm and Google for data center chips, while the British firm is also expanding beyond licensing into production, beginning with the new AGI central processing unit (CPU), according to Fujitsu Research India.Sharma said the Unified Acceleration (UXL) Foundation, hosted by the Linux Foundation's Joint Development Foundation (JDF), demonstrates that the semiconductor industry is “realising the importance of Arm”.The UXL Foundation comprises Intel, Arm, Qualcomm, Samsung Electronics, Imagination Technologies, Fujitsu, Google Cloud, and AMD as steering members.“The software ecosystem of Arm has matured, and it is growing very fast as compared to the other ecosystems because people are realising the need for energy-efficient data centers,” the executive said.Fujitsu, whose expertise spans IT services to hardware, is expected to launch its MONAKA-X CPU based on a 1.4-nanometer (nm) node in the next two years, paired with neural processing units (NPUs) for accelerated AI processing, Sharma said.She underscored that the Indian government is also emphasising Arm-based data centers for a variety of government-related applications and ecosystem.“The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) has recently come up with Arm-based chips. In fact, CDAC has also become one of the general members of the UXL Foundation, so they are also interested in contributing to this ecosystem,” Sharma concluded.

stories.title: BTC Digital inks tripartite MOU to explore building AI data center in Vietnam
stories.summary: Singapore-based BTC Digital has signed a tripartite MOU with Vietnam's Nam Trang Cat Investment and Development JSC and SG Partners to explore developing an AI data center in Hai Phong, with a proposed site already identified. The project remains at an exploratory stage.
stories.why_it_matters: The agreement adds to a growing pipeline of foreign-backed AI data center proposals in northern Vietnam, where Hai Phong is emerging as an alternative hub to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. It signals that smaller regional players, not just hyperscalers, are racing to secure sites and local partners ahead of Vietnam's regulatory and power frameworks fully taking shape.
stories.content:
Singapore-based computing infrastructure firm BTC Digital Ltd. recently announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Nam Trang Cat Investment and Development Joint Stock Company (NTC) and SG Partners Co., Limited (SGP) to explore building an artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) project in Hai Phong, Vietnam.

The proposed site has been identified as being within the 2 million square meters Nam Trang Cat Industrial Park in Hai Phong. The parties plan to undertake feasibility studies on site suitability, power-access verification, network and cooling design, permitting, customer-demand validation, and financing and investment planning. The site has a planned power load of about 300MW, as per NTC.

Under the MOU, NTC will take care of local project coordination and assist with verification of relevant site, power and infrastructure conditions, while BTC Digital will contribute its digital computing infrastructure experience and international business resources, to project evaluation and technical preparation. SGP is expected to engage with potential investors and industry participants.

The two-year MOU includes an initial six-month exclusivity period and is subject to a definitive agreement being signed, according to BTC Digital’s press release.

Siguang Peng, Chief Executive Officer of BTC Digital Ltd. said: “This MOU gives the parties a practical framework for the next stage of work: verifying the site and power profile, completing the technical design, mapping permitting requirements and evaluating the project’s capital structure. We intend to advance the Hai Phong opportunity in stages and make investment or construction decisions only after the key conditions have been validated.”

stories.title: ASML extends chipmaking dominance as customers embrace High NA
stories.summary: Customer commitments suggest Europe’s most valuable company can continue its dominance in chip-printing lithography machines into the 2030s
stories.content:
Customer commitments suggest Europe’s most valuable company can continue its dominance in chip-printing lithography machines into the 2030s

[AMSTERDAM] As Dutch computer chip equipment maker ASML broke ground on a new plant in Eindhoven last week, CFO Roger Dassen said the artificial intelligence boom had transformed the mood among customers.

Its existing US$200 million extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines, essential for making advanced AI chips, are all but sold out through 2027, while customers have made a flurry of commitments to adopt its next generation of US$400 million High NA (numerical aperture) tools.

“Can you give me more? Can you give it to me fast?“ was the tone of one recent conversation with a major customer, Dassen said.

TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix all set dates to begin using High NA in production, while early adopter Intel said that the machines are already meeting throughput and reliability standards. Together with the new capacity plans, the developments suggest Europe’s most valuable company can continue its dominance in chip-printing lithography machines into the 2030s.

“I don’t think we’re at the end of (the AI boom), to be honest,” CEO Christophe Fouquet told Reuters by phone.

ASML’s customers include all major chipmakers, notably Taiwan’s TSMC, which produces chips for Apple and Nvidia. TSMC had previously questioned whether High NA justified its US$400 million price tag, but has now committed to using the technology from 2030.

Chipmakers spent years evaluating whether advances in chip packaging, three-dimensional stacking and other manufacturing techniques could reduce the need for High NA.

The commitments suggest the industry’s biggest players still expect shrinking chip features will be needed to improve performance.

High NA can print features about 40 per cent smaller than standard EUV systems, potentially cutting manufacturing steps and increasing productivity – but it costs roughly twice as much.

## Monopoly power

JPMorgan estimates ASML held a 94 per cent share of the global lithography market in 2025.

At the cutting edge, its position is stronger still: ASML has had a monopoly since the late 2010s on machines that use extreme ultraviolet light needed to create the smallest circuitry in the most powerful commercial AI chips.

High NA, first shipped in 2023, is the next generation of EUV tech.

ASML has no commercial rival in EUV. Japan’s Nikon and Canon, along with emerging Chinese competitors, make systems using deep ultraviolet light, an older technology. Morningstar analyst Javier Correonero said fears that these firms are close to catching up to ASML in lithography amount to “misinformation”.

## Chip industry aligns around new tool

The trillion-dollar global semiconductor industry makes investment decisions years before chips reach production, with manufacturers, equipment suppliers and materials firms coordinating so that new tools, chemicals and processes work together.

Some experts had questioned whether chipmakers would adopt High NA widely enough to justify its development costs.

“I’ve never doubted it, because there was no alternative,” said InsingerGilissen analyst Jos Versteeg.

Samsung said it will start memory chip production with High NA tools in 2028, which Morningstar’s Correonero said was earlier than the market expected.

Memory specialist SK Hynix also announced it will use High NA from 2028, while Micron has ordered tools but not set a date for using them in production.

Intel, the first adopter, said recently that it has now processed more than a million wafers with High NA tools.

Fouquet said that the threshold for memory firms to adopt High NA was lower, due to the smaller size of their finished chips.

“You see a bit more aggressiveness in the plans of those guys on many things, that includes High NA,” he said. “All of them are moving forward with plans to adopt High NA in high-volume manufacturing.” REUTERS
